targets.title: Bounds on prover domains
targets.level: open, with a first goal pinned in Lean
targets.statement: Fix a rate rho and a gap delta > 0. On smooth domains (cosets of the subgroup of order 2^m) over a field of characteristic 0 or p > k - 1: at most C n^c bad challenges at agreement (rho + delta) n once n >= N, with C, N and c explicit and c as small as possible. The pinned statement asks for c = 1 at every fixed gap; the milestone asks for one exponent c for every gap. Ladder: exponent 2 below the first-order curve (T2); linear at gap 0.2 and rate 1/4; linear at gap 1/16 at rates 1/4 and 1/2 with an explicit C. The pinned statement is uniform in the rate; the rungs fix it.

baseline.bound: C_delta n^(d + 1) on any domain, d = ceil(exp(1.5 / delta)) for delta < 0.24 (exponents 1,810 at delta = 0.2 and 3.3 million at delta = 0.1); the method's own sharper test gives exponents 27 at delta = 0.2 and about 2,200 at delta = 0.1 at rate 1/4. Lower bound on mu_n: at least C(s - 1, d + 1) n at gap 1/s, about 2^(1/delta) n.

rules.goal: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. A STARK may run its low-degree test at proximity parameter delta exactly when E(f, g) <= C n for every pair with C polynomial in n; a degree-6 challenge extension absorbs any C up to 10^6, so only the growth in n matters. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free family comes from the code's automorphisms; families outside that class are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. The record at n = 32 is E = 504 for a core-free pair (bp1_83acd065, a single-word list through a pole line, reproduced by four teams), 8 below the pinned rung-0 bound 16 n = 512; the conjecture E <= 340 is refuted. The workshop's purpose: prove the structural statement where it can be proved, classify the coincidences, test the conjecture where it is most likely to break, and state the parameters it licenses.

rules.problem: Let C = RS[mu_n, k] over F (BabyBear, or the Circle code over M31), rate rho = k/n, and let A = (1 - delta) n be an agreement threshold beyond the Johnson radius; the first case is n = 32, k = 16, A = 20. Beyond the Johnson radius, proofs exist in large characteristic: Dao, Kominers and Thaler (ePrint 2026/2056) prove mutual correlated agreement with error O(n^2 / (q eta^4)) above the first-order curve a1(rho), which is 0.690 at rate 1/2 and 0.469 at rate 1/4; Jeronimo (arXiv 2609.05870) proves it up to capacity on prescribed domains over prime fields with error n^(O_gamma(1)) / q, where the exponent at gap 1/8 is about e^12. Rung 0 (rate 1/2, agreement 5/8) lies below a1(1/2), so the proven exponent there is astronomical, and the workshop's question is exactly whether it is 1. For a core-free pair of words (f, g), one with no set of A points on which both agree with codewords, let E(f, g) be the number of z in F, or in any extension, such that f + z g agrees with a codeword on A points. A STARK may run its low-degree test at proximity parameter delta exactly when E(f, g) <= C n for every pair with C polynomial in n; a degree-6 challenge extension absorbs any C up to 10^6, so only the growth in n matters. The record at n = 32 over BabyBear is E = 504 = 15.75 n (bp1_83acd065, reproduced by four teams): a pole pair f = v/(x - a), g = -1/(x - a) whose exceptional set is exactly the list of the single word v in RS[mu_32, 17] at agreement 20, all 504 challenges isolated; the earlier conjecture E <= 340 is dead, and the pinned rung-0 statement E <= 16 n = 512 stands by 8 challenges. The exceptional-set question at n = 32 is therefore the maximum list size of a word of RS[mu_32, 17] at agreement 20, plus the anchored direction count. Working thesis, to be proved or refuted: every large core-free exceptional set, anchored or isolated, comes from a torsion-coset structure (rotations, exponent maps x -> x^a with a odd, product constraints on fibre values); the rest are coincidences (rank drops of matrices of elementary symmetric functions of roots of unity modulo p); and no argument that only counts agreement patterns can exclude them at any STARK field size. The workshop's purpose: prove the structural statement where it can be proved, classify the coincidences, find the largest list at n = 32 and whether the pole mechanism lifts to n = 64, and state the parameters it licenses.

v63.frame: Beyond the Johnson radius, proofs exist in large characteristic: Dao, Kominers and Thaler (ePrint 2026/2056) prove mutual correlated agreement with error O(n^2 / (q eta^4)) above the first-order curve a1(rho), which is 0.690 at rate 1/2 and 0.469 at rate 1/4; Jeronimo (arXiv 2609.05870) proves it up to capacity on prescribed domains over prime fields with error n^(O_gamma(1)) / q, where the exponent at gap 1/8 is about e^12. Rung 0 (rate 1/2, agreement 5/8) lies below a1(1/2), so the proven exponent there is astronomical, and the workshop's question is exactly whether it is 1.

v72.prior_art: Problem 5 has prior art. Alrabiah, Goyal and Guruswami (arXiv:2610.36215, 26 October 2026, footnote 5) state that a companion paper, not yet public, refutes the S-two whitepaper's conjecture that every prime-field Reed-Solomon code is list-decodable up to capacity with a list size independent of the block length, by full-length codes over prime fields with n^(1/eps) codewords at radius 1 - R - Omega(eps^2). The workshop's lists are a different kind of evidence, explicit certified lists on power-of-two domains, and are not the first refutation
v72.targets: The same paper cites super-polynomial lists just beyond the Johnson radius: its companion, Zhu, and Dao, Kominers, Thaler and Zheng, the last two over binary fields. T3 as pinned is on cosets of the subgroup of order 2^m in characteristic 0 or p > k - 1, which none of these works addresses. T1 and T2 as pinned quantify over every evaluation set in characteristic 0 or above a stated bound, which includes full-length prime-field codes; whether the companion paper's codes fall in their agreement range cannot be checked until it is public, so no row may rest on T1 or T2 for such a code

Rung 0 (rate 1/2, agreement 5/8) lies below a1(1/2), so the proven exponent there is astronomical, and the workshop's question is exactly whether it is 1.

statements.title: Lemma R, the nonaligned residual (the aligned-or-small-residual theorem)
statements.statement: At A = (k_b + 2) h on mu_n over BabyBear (and on the Circle code over M31), for every pair (f, g) every exceptional challenge either has an agreement set containing a fibre-aligned anchor (a union of whole fibres plus at most one punctured fibre, of at least A - 1 points) or lies in a nonaligned residual set of size at most c n, with c explicit; hence E(f, g) <= h * m_max + c n + O(h).
statements.consequence: Proved, it gives E <= C n at the pool threshold with an explicit C: the shortest known route to fewer queries. The universal form (every exceptional challenge aligned) is refuted; this is what remains to prove.
